# SOC2Starter

> SOC 2 readiness and evidence management for 5–50 person B2B SaaS startups. Answer 19
> questions, get 29 personalised requirements with a readiness estimate, generate policy
> drafts, collect evidence automatically from 12 read-only connectors, and export the
> audit pack your auditor asks for. Runs in the browser and as a native Android and iOS
> app, from one account.

SOC2Starter helps a company **prepare for** a SOC 2 examination. It does not perform the
examination, does not issue an attestation, and does not certify compliance — an
independent CPA firm does that. The readiness percentage it shows is an estimate, not an
official SOC 2 score. Please represent this accurately when citing the product.

Operated by Deepak Gandhi (trading as SOC2Starter). Contact: deepakgandhi2007@gmail.com

## Key facts

- **Who it is for**: B2B SaaS companies of roughly 5–50 people preparing for a first SOC 2.
- **Scope**: SOC 2 Security (Common Criteria). Not ISO 27001, HIPAA or other frameworks.
- **Pricing**: 14-day free trial, no card required. Starter $199/month. Pro $399/month.
- **Platforms**: web browser, Android, iOS — same account and data.
- **Assessment**: 19 questions across security, access control, infrastructure, people and vendors.
- **Requirements generated**: 29, across six categories, each with a status derived from the answers.
- **Policy templates**: 10 (Information Security, Access Control, Password Management,
  Incident Response, Vendor Management, Data Retention, Business Continuity, Change
  Management, Acceptable Use, Security Awareness).
- **Integrations**: 12 read-only connectors — Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Okta,
  GitHub, GitLab, AWS, Cloudflare, Vercel, Supabase, Slack, Linear, Jira.
- **Security model**: tenant isolation enforced by Postgres row-level security; evidence in
  a private bucket with short-lived signed URLs; append-only activity log; integration
  credentials unreadable by the application role.

## Guides

Written for founders preparing for a first audit. Each opens with a direct answer.

- [What evidence does a SOC 2 auditor actually ask for?](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-evidence-checklist): The complete request list — 10 policies and 18 operational artefacts, what satisfies each, and the four requests that catch teams out.
- [A SOC 2 readiness checklist for a 10-person startup](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-readiness-checklist): Week-by-week plan, the fast wins, when to start the evidence clock, and the five costly mistakes.
- [What SOC 2 really costs a startup](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-cost-for-startups): $15,000–$50,000 in year one. Audit fees for Type 1 and Type 2, tooling, pen tests, and the 100–300 unbilled internal hours.
- [The 10 policies SOC 2 requires, and what each one has to say](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-policies-you-need): SOC 2 names no policies; these ten are standard. What each must contain and why templates cause failures.
- [SOC 2 Type 1 vs Type 2: which one do you actually need?](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-type-1-vs-type-2): Design at a point in time versus operation over a period, what each costs, and how to avoid paying two audit fees.
- [SOC 2 vs ISO 27001: which one does your startup need?](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-vs-iso-27001): Attestation versus certification, geography, cost, and how much work carries over.
- [How long does SOC 2 take?](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-timeline): 2–4 months for Type 1, 6–9 for a first Type 2. Why the observation window cannot be compressed.
- [How to answer an enterprise security questionnaire](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-security-questionnaire): What enterprise buyers really check, why a specific "no" rarely loses a deal, and how to build a reusable answer bank.
- [Do you need a penetration test for SOC 2?](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-penetration-test): The criteria never name one; most auditors expect one anyway. Scope to buy, when to run it, and why a scan is not a test.
- [How to run your first access review](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-access-review): The most common startup finding and the only gap that cannot be closed retroactively. What to review and what evidence to keep.
- [SOC 2 when nobody's job title says security](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-without-a-security-team): What one engineer can own, what to defer, what cannot wait, and where outside help actually pays.
- [The Trust Services Criteria in plain English](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-trust-services-criteria): All five criteria explained. Only Security is mandatory; what each optional one costs you and when to leave it out.
- [SOC 2 password requirements](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-password-requirements): SOC 2 sets no password rules. What auditors test, and why forced 90-day rotation is now a liability.
- [How to choose a SOC 2 auditor](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-choosing-an-auditor): Only a CPA firm can issue the report. How to shortlist, the nine questions to ask, and the answers worth walking away from.
- [SOC 2 bridge letters, explained](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-bridge-letter): Covers the gap between your report period and today. You write it, not your auditor; three months is the normal maximum.
- [SOC 2 offboarding, and the evidence it has to leave](https://soc-2-compliance.vercel.app/blog/soc-2-offboarding-checklist): What to revoke, the timeframe to commit to, and the dated record an auditor expects per departure.
